articles.body:
Page 7, "Looming Crisis" says: 
[q=Looming Crisis]When the Elephant is placed on a border between two regions, the acting region (with the Elephant's tail) is getting ready to invade the region the Elephant faces.[/q]

Page 32, "Crisis / Rebellion" says:
[q=Rebellion]If the attacker is a dominated region, resolve a Rebellion.[/q]

This second rule seems to indicate that even if the Elephant is pointing at a Company region from a dominated region, there is no risk of Invasion; the crisis will always be Rebellion. (This caught us off guard as we were expecting to be invaded.) Is this correct?

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xml><safehtml>Page 7, "Looming Crisis" says: <br/></safehtml><quote><qauthor><safehtml>Looming Crisis</safehtml></qauthor><qbody><safehtml>When the Elephant is placed on a border between two regions, the acting region (with the Elephant's tail) is getting ready to invade the region the Elephant faces.</safehtml></qbody></quote><safehtml>Page 32, "Crisis / Rebellion" says:<br/></safehtml><quote userid="239403"><qauthor><safehtml>rebellion</safehtml></qauthor><qbody><safehtml>If the attacker is a dominated region, resolve a Rebellion.</safehtml></qbody></quote><safehtml>This second rule seems to indicate that even if the Elephant is pointing at a Company region from a dominated region, there is no risk of Invasion; the crisis will always be Rebellion. (This caught us off guard as we were expecting to be invaded.) Is this correct?</safehtml></xml>

articles.body:
The second quote only applies if the attacker is a dominated region.  Specifically, if it is a territory with a small flag pointing at the capital (big flag).  This is a rebellion.

If the attacker is Sovereign (either the capital of an empire, or not part of an empire), then it is instead an Invasion.

For example:
[q]Situation: Punjab is Sovereign, and Bombay is company controlled

If the elephant is on the border between the two, pointing from Punjab to Bombay, then this would be an Invasion Crisis that the company would need to worry about.[/q]

articles.body:
[q="Samuel Vriezen"]I don’t think it’s possible for a dominated region to threaten the Company?[/q]
This is correct, because anytime a Dominated region is chosen, it always targets the capital region for a rebellion.

Also note that Company Controlled regions are technically considered "Dominated", though I wish Cole had just made a separate category for them.

articles.body:
Page 32 doesn't really apply here.  Rebellion can only happen in two places, when the elephant's tail is in a dominated region and it's face is pointing to it's capital.  Or when the elephant is fully contained in a region (such as the company).  Intuatively this should make sense.  

In your case, it would be that empire's full strength (capital flag + dominated flags combined tower levels) + crisis modifier + unrest all against your company's army.

Anybody feel free to correct me if i'm wrong.

Also note that Company Controlled regions are technically considered "Dominated", though I wish Cole had just made a separate category for them.[/q]

For what purpose? 

In the Elephant's March it clearly is delineated what happens if it lands in a company controlled region vs if it lands in a dominated region.  So what purpose would grouping them together serve? maybe I misunderstood something you wrote.

This is my point.  Company controlled regions are already defined as "dominated" regions within the rules, and it makes this more confusing IMHO:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/AALQqhn.png[/img]

There should be 3 political alignments: Sovereign, Subjugated, or Company Controlled.  Then if you want, you could call any region which is Subjugated or Company controlled to be equal to 'dominated' if the term was truly needed.
